title: Weekly beer line cleaning with Pipeline Purple and a cleaning bottle
summary: A step-by-step routine for cleaning draught lines at least every seven days using Pipeline Purple powder, a cleaning bottle or cleaning sockets. Covers preparation, contact time, rinsing and record keeping.
body: Beer lines should be cleaned at least every seven days. Yeast, protein and beer stone build up quickly inside the tubing, and even a few extra days can lead to hazy beer, off flavours and fobbing. Pick a quiet time, tell the bar team, and hang a notice on each tap you are cleaning so nobody serves from a line that contains cleaning solution.

Before you start, put on chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection. Read the instructions on the Pipeline Purple sachet and make up the solution with clean cold water at exactly the dilution the chemical supplier specifies. Never mix it with other cleaning products and never use hot water unless the supplier's instructions allow it.

Turn off the secondary regulator or gas supply to the lines being cleaned, lift the coupler handle and remove the coupler from the keg. Fit the coupler to a cleaning socket connected to your water supply, or to a cleaning bottle with the lid that matches your coupler type. Draw clean water through each tap until it runs clear to push out the remaining beer.

Fill the cleaning bottle with the made-up solution, reconnect the gas, and draw solution through each line until it arrives at the tap. Close the tap and leave the solution to stand for the contact time stated by the chemical supplier. Partway through, draw a little more fresh solution through to disturb any deposits.

Rinse the system thoroughly with clean water until no trace of the cleaner remains at the tap. Use the check method recommended by the chemical supplier, and taste a small sample of the water before reconnecting kegs. Clean the coupler, keg spears and tap nozzles separately while the lines are rinsing.

Reconnect the kegs, pull beer through until it runs clear and at a normal head, and discard the first product. Record the date, lines cleaned and the name of the person who carried out the clean in your cellar log so the next clean is not missed.

title: Choosing the right keg coupler: A, D, G, S, U and KeyKeg
summary: How to identify the fitting on a keg and pick the matching coupler. Each coupler type fits only its own keg valve, so getting this right avoids leaks, damage and wasted product.
body: A keg coupler connects your gas supply and beer line to the valve (spear) in the top of the keg. Each coupler type is made for one valve design only. Forcing the wrong coupler onto a keg can damage the spear and seals, cause leaks, or fail to open the valve at all.

The S type (Sankey) is the most common coupler in UK bars and is used by many major lager, ale and cider brands. The A type suits a flat-profile valve used by a number of European breweries. The G type fits Grundy kegs, which are still found on some cask-conditioned and traditional brands. The D type and U type each fit their own valve designs, and the KeyKeg coupler is for KeyKeg one-way kegs only.

The simplest way to confirm the type is to ask the brewery or distributor, as the coupler type is usually stated on the delivery note or product information. If you are unsure, compare the keg valve with a keg you already dispense or send Brewfitt technical support a clear photo of the top of the keg.

Brewfitt couplers are supplied with JG push-fit fittings and, apart from the KeyKeg coupler, a non-return valve (NRV). The NRV stops beer from travelling back up the gas line, which protects your regulators and gas ring main. Check the NRV is present and working whenever you service a coupler.

If you run several brands with different coupler types, label each coupler and keep a matching cleaning socket or cleaning bottle for every type in use, so line cleaning can be carried out on every line without improvising.

title: Setting primary and secondary regulators for CO2 and mixed gas
summary: The difference between primary and secondary regulators, how to match a primary regulator to CO2 or mixed gas, and a safe sequence for setting dispense pressure for each brand.
body: A primary regulator connects to the gas cylinder and reduces the high cylinder pressure to a steady distribution pressure for the cellar ring main. Secondary regulators are then fitted on the ring main, usually one per brand, to set the exact top pressure each keg needs. Brewfitt stocks primary regulators for CO2 rated at 45 PSI and for mixed gas rated at 55 PSI, in bottle-mounted and wall-mounted versions.

Always use a primary regulator that is designed for the gas in the cylinder. CO2 regulators must only be used on CO2 cylinders and mixed gas regulators only on mixed gas cylinders. Never adapt fittings to make a regulator fit a cylinder it was not designed for, and never set a regulator above its rated pressure.

To fit a primary regulator, check the cylinder is chained upright and the cylinder valve is closed. Inspect the regulator seal, fit the regulator by hand and tighten it with the correct spanner without over-tightening. Make sure the regulator is wound fully out, then open the cylinder valve slowly and watch the contents gauge.

Wind the primary regulator in gradually until the outlet gauge reads the distribution pressure recommended for your installation. Then set each secondary regulator for its brand. The correct dispense pressure depends on the product, its carbonation, cellar temperature and line length, so follow the brewery's recommendation or ask Brewfitt technical support rather than guessing.

After any change, check every joint with a suitable gas leak detection spray and watch the gauges for a few minutes with the taps closed. A falling reading points to a leak. Carbon dioxide can build up in enclosed cellars, so make sure the cellar is ventilated and that any gas detection equipment on site is working.

title: Storing and securing gas cylinders in the cellar with a twin gas bottle holder
summary: Practical rules for keeping CO2 and mixed gas cylinders upright, chained and separated in a cellar, including where to mount the twin gas bottle holder and how to handle cylinder changes.
body: Gas cylinders hold gas at high pressure and are heavy. A cylinder that falls can snap off its valve or regulator and cause serious injury. Every cylinder in use or in store should stand upright and be secured with a chain or strap to a solid wall or fixed rack.

Mount the twin gas bottle holder on a sound wall at a height where the chain passes around the upper part of the cylinders. Use fixings suitable for the wall construction and seek professional advice if you are unsure. Keep the area clear so cylinders can be moved in and out without lifting them over other equipment.

Store cylinders away from heat sources, cooler condensers and direct sunlight, and keep them out of walkways and escape routes. Separate full and empty cylinders and label them clearly so an empty cylinder is not connected by mistake. Only keep the number of spare cylinders on site that you actually need.

When changing a cylinder, close the cylinder valve, release the pressure using the regulator or shut-off valve, and remove the regulator before releasing the chain. Secure the new cylinder with the chain before fitting the regulator, then open the valve slowly and check for leaks.

Never roll a cylinder on its side, drag it by the valve, or leave it standing unsecured, even for a moment. Carbon dioxide and nitrogen are both asphyxiants, so keep the cellar ventilated and report any suspected leak straight away.

title: Choosing between Coolflow DTX, 2FLOW+ and 4FLOW+ and topping up coolant
summary: How the coolants in the Brewfitt range differ, which form to buy for your system, and a safe routine for checking and topping up coolant in a remote cooler.
body: Remote coolers circulate a coolant through the python to keep beer cold from the cellar to the font. Using the right coolant at the right strength protects the system from freezing, helps it run efficiently and reduces corrosion. Always check which coolant your cooler and python were commissioned with before buying more.

Coolflow DTX is a non-toxic coolant supplied either as a concentrate, in 5 and 25 litre containers, or as a 28 percent pre-mix. The concentrate must be diluted with clean water to the ratio given by the manufacturer for your system. The pre-mix is ready to use and removes the risk of mixing errors, which makes it a sensible choice for routine top-ups.

2FLOW+ and 4FLOW+ are specialist coolants intended for systems designed around them, typically installations serving extra-cold products. Do not switch an existing system to a specialist coolant, or mix different coolant types, without advice. Mixing products can change freeze protection and performance, and the system may need to be drained and flushed first.

To top up, isolate the cooler's electrical supply, remove the reservoir lid and check the level against the marks given in the cooler manufacturer's instructions. Add the correct coolant slowly until the level is right, refit the lid and restore power. Wear gloves and eye protection when handling concentrate, and wipe up any spills.

If you find yourself topping up regularly, there is probably a leak in the python, a fitting or the cooler itself. Look for wet insulation, drips under the font or ice build-up, and contact Brewfitt technical support rather than continuing to add coolant.

title: Fitting a beer font to the bar top with the correct clamp assembly
summary: How to choose between the clamp assemblies in the range and fit a font securely without drilling fixing holes in the bar top.
body: A clamp assembly holds a font to the counter by clamping above and below the bar top through a single opening, rather than bolting the font through several drilled holes. This means a font can later be moved or replaced without leaving extra holes in the bar.

Choose the clamp to suit the font. Towers with three or more dispense points, and towers that use recirculation, use the black clamp assemblies with a 75 mm opening. Cobra fonts use the Cobra clamp assembly, and ceramic towers such as the Giada use the hexagonal clamp, which is designed to spread the load on a ceramic base. If the font is not listed, ask Brewfitt which clamp it needs before cutting the counter.

Mark the position of the font so that taps sit centrally over the drip tray and staff have room to hold a glass under every tap. Cut the opening to the size needed for the clamp and python, check below the counter for cables and pipes before cutting, and clean up any sharp edges.

Feed the product lines, python and any LED cable through the opening, taking care not to kink the lines or crush the insulation. Sit the font on the counter, fit the lower clamp plate from underneath and tighten the fixings evenly, a little at a time, until the font is firm. Do not over-tighten, particularly on ceramic towers.

Connect the lines as described in the font and cooler instructions, then check for leaks and run a line clean before the font goes into service. Recheck the clamp fixings after the first week, as the counter surface can settle slightly.

title: Connecting a drip tray glass freshener to the mains water supply
summary: How to connect a glass freshener using the mains water connection kit and its pressure reducer, plus simple checks and maintenance to keep the rinser working.
body: A glass freshener is a spring-loaded rinser in the drip tray. Pressing a glass down onto it releases a short spray of cold water that rinses and cools the glass before it is filled. It needs a mains cold water supply and a drain to waste.

The glass freshener connection kit includes a stem elbow, a tube fitting, blue water pipework and a pressure reducer rated up to a maximum of 3 bar. The reducer is important: mains pressure varies between sites and can be high enough to cause splashing or to strain the freshener seals.

Take the supply from a cold mains branch with an accessible isolating valve. The connection must comply with the water supply regulations, including suitable backflow protection, so use a qualified plumber if you are not sure. Fit the pressure reducer in the supply line, run the blue pipework to the freshener without tight bends, and push the tube fully into each fitting.

Connect the drip tray drain to a suitable waste using the drain kit, with a fall along its whole length so water does not sit in the tray. Turn the water on slowly and check every joint for leaks, then press a glass onto the freshener several times to confirm an even spray.

If the freshener sticks, leaks or sprays weakly, isolate the water and check for debris or worn parts. The repair kit contains the spring, pin and washers for Celli glass fresheners, and a complete replacement freshener is available for existing trays.

title: Fitting badge holders, tap adapters, ring spacers and LED boards on a tower
summary: Which parts you need to fit a brand badge to a tower tap point, when to use the tap adapter or ring spacer, and how illuminated badge holders are powered.
body: Badge holders carry the brand badge above each tap. Standard, extended and side-arm holders are available in chrome and gold, and can be used on most towers in the Brewfitt range and on T bars.

When a badge holder is fitted to a tower, a 1/2 inch male to 1/2 inch female tap adapter is needed. The adapter extends the tap point so that the badge holder can sit over it and the tap still screws on fully. The same adapter can be used on keg walls where the wall is thick and extra length is needed.

If an FC4 tap is fitted to a tower without a badge holder, fit a chrome ring spacer instead. It covers the exposed part of the backshaft so the installation looks finished and the thread is protected.

Brand badges are stuck to solid or LED badge holders using round double-sided sticky pads. Clean and dry the face of the holder first, centre the badge and press it firmly for a few seconds. Replace the pad whenever a badge is changed rather than reusing the old one.

Towers with domed illuminated badge holders use an LED board. Low-voltage lighting is powered from a 240/24V bar lighting transformer, which should be installed by a competent electrician in a ventilated position away from water. Always isolate the transformer before working on any lighting.

title: Setting up a Lindr Kontakt or Pygmy unit for an event
summary: A practical checklist for siting, connecting and starting a Lindr mobile dispense unit at a party, festival or pop-up bar, from gas and keg connection to the first pour.
body: Lindr Kontakt and Pygmy units are compact dispensers that chill beer on its way from the keg to the tap, which makes them well suited to events and temporary bars. Before the event, confirm which keg couplers you need, that you have enough gas, and that a suitable power socket is available close to the serving position.

Place the unit on a stable, level surface out of direct sunlight, with the ventilation openings clear on all sides. The cooling system needs free airflow to work properly, so do not push the unit against a wall or cover it with cloths or branding.

Connect the gas cylinder through a suitable regulator, chain or otherwise secure the cylinder upright, and connect the keg couplers to the product inlets. Switch the unit on and allow it to reach operating temperature as described in the Lindr instructions before you start serving.

Set the dispense pressure to suit the product and check the first pours. If the beer is fobbing, check the gas pressure and temperature before changing anything else. Keep kegs in the shade and as cool as practical, because very warm kegs are harder for a portable unit to bring down to serving temperature.
Brewfitt recommends buying a cleaning bottle with every Lindr unit. Clean the lines before first use and after each event, following the routine in the Lindr cleaning and transport guide.

title: Choosing a Gamko Maxiglass bottle cooler: hinged or sliding doors
summary: Points to consider when choosing an under-counter bottle cooler, including capacity, door style, hinge side and the space available behind the bar.
body: The Gamko Maxiglass range covers single-door 150 litre models and two and three door models of 250, 275 and 315 litres. Start by measuring the space under the back bar, allowing for the ventilation clearances given in the manufacturer's installation instructions, and by estimating how many bottles you need to hold chilled at your busiest times.

Hinged doors open fully, which makes loading and cleaning easier. On single-door models you choose a left or right hand hinge, so check which side staff will stand and which way the door should swing so it does not block a walkway or clash with a neighbouring cooler or glass washer.

Sliding doors do not swing out into the service area. They suit narrow back bars and busy positions where an open hinged door would get in the way. Only part of the cooler can be open at a time, which should be considered when you plan loading.

Glass-door models let staff see stock before opening the door and help customers see what is available. Several models also have a range of finishes and door options, shown in the model code. Check the full product description or ask Brewfitt to confirm the exact variant before ordering.
Once installed, keep the condenser area free from dust and boxes, and avoid overloading shelves so cold air can circulate. Isolate the power before cleaning inside the cabinet or behind the unit.

title: How CoolTube cools beer at the point of dispense
summary: An explanation of CoolTube compact heat exchangers, where they sit in a dispense system and what to consider when planning an installation.
body: CoolTube is a compact heat exchanger fitted close to the point of dispense. The product line runs through the CoolTube, and coolant taken from the python recirculation lines flows around it. Heat passes from the beer into the coolant, so the product is chilled again just before it reaches the tap.

Because the final cooling happens near the font, CoolTube can help deliver a colder and more consistent pint on long runs where the product would otherwise warm up. The 4 way models serve four lines, and with an additional valve they allow different dispense temperatures for different products.

CoolTube works with any coolant medium, so it can be added to existing dispense systems without changing the coolant. It does depend on a working remote cooler and python recirculation, as it has no refrigeration of its own.

The Pancake CoolTube is a flatter design for primary and secondary cooling where space under the counter or in the font is limited. Single and 4 way versions are available in 10 line and 15 line sizes, with or without fittings, and the tubular models come with PU insulation.

When planning an installation, confirm the line sizes, available space and coolant flow at the font. Insulate all connections to prevent condensation, and have the system commissioned by a competent dispense technician.

title: Preparing a Lindr CWP Green Line mobile tower for an outdoor event
summary: Filling, positioning and starting a CWP mobile water cooler tower for an outdoor bar, and draining it safely afterwards for transport.
body: CWP Green Line mobile towers are water-based coolers built into a mobile unit with a dispense tower and drip tray. They are designed for larger events, fairs and sports venues where a full cellar installation is not practical.

Before travelling, check the unit for damage, confirm the taps and couplers are clean and that you have a cleaning bottle, gas, regulator and suitable couplers for the kegs being served. Plan where the unit will stand so it is level, shaded where possible, and close to a suitable weatherproof power supply.

On site, fill the cooler with clean water to the level shown on the water gauge, following the Lindr instructions. Allow the unit to run and build up its cooling before service starts. The time needed depends on the model and the ambient temperature, so plan to arrive early.
Secure the gas cylinder upright, connect the regulator and couplers, and check the first pours for temperature and head. Keep kegs out of direct sun during the day.

After the event, clean the product lines, switch off and disconnect the power, and use the drain valve to empty the water before moving the unit. Transporting a CWP with water in it adds weight and risks spills and damage.

title: Troubleshooting fobbing, cloudy beer and warm pints
summary: Answers to the most common draught quality complaints, with the checks to make in the cellar before calling for a technician.
body: Q: Why is every pint fobbing? A: The most common causes are beer that is too warm, gas pressure that is set too high or too low, or dirty lines. Check the cellar temperature and the remote cooler first, then check that the secondary regulator for that brand is set to the recommended pressure, and confirm when the lines were last cleaned.

Q: Only the first pint after a quiet period fobs. Is that a fault? A: Beer sitting in the line and font can warm up between pours, particularly on long runs or where the python recirculation is not reaching the font. Check the python insulation and coolant flow. If the problem continues, ask Brewfitt technical support whether point of dispense cooling would help.

Q: The beer looks hazy or cloudy. What should I check? A: Check the product is within its date and has been stored at the right temperature, and that the keg has not been disturbed. Then look at line hygiene: hazy beer and off flavours are often the first sign that lines have gone too long without cleaning. Clean lines at least every seven days.

Q: Pints are coming out warm. What can I do before calling a technician? A: Check the cooler is switched on and running, that the fans and condenser are not blocked by boxes or dust, and that the coolant level in the reservoir is correct. Isolate the power before removing any covers. If the cooler is running but the beer is still warm, contact Brewfitt technical support.

Q: We lose a lot of beer each time a keg runs out. How can we reduce this? A: When a keg empties, gas and foam enter the line and the fob has to be pulled off before the new keg pours properly. A foam stop fitted at the coupler reduces the amount of gas and foam that escapes into the line, which reduces waste at keg changes.

Q: Should I change the gas pressure to fix fobbing? A: Only change pressure as a last resort and only within the brewery's recommended range. Changing pressure to mask a temperature or cleaning problem usually causes over or under carbonated beer later.

title: Foam Stop and FOB detection: common questions
summary: What a foam stop does, where it fits and how it compares with a conventional FOB detector.
body: Q: What does the Foam Stop do? A: It is a compact device that connects to a standard keg coupler. As the keg empties, it greatly reduces the amount of gas and foam that escapes from the keg into the beer line, so less beer is wasted when the keg is changed.

Q: How is that different from a FOB detector? A: A FOB (foam on beer) detector is usually a float chamber fitted in the beer line that closes when it fills with foam, keeping the line full of beer until the keg is changed and the detector is reset. The Foam Stop works at the coupler instead. Both aim to reduce waste at keg changes, and Brewfitt technical support can advise which suits your system.
Q: Which systems can it be used on? A: It is intended for installations using CO2 or mixed CO2 and nitrogen, and has a 1/2 inch G by 1/2 inch BSP connection to fit a standard keg coupler.
Q: Does it need cleaning? A: Yes. It is part of the product path, so include it in your line cleaning routine at least every seven days and inspect it whenever you service the coupler.

Q: Will it fix fobbing during normal pouring? A: No. It reduces waste as a keg runs out. Fobbing during normal service is usually caused by temperature, pressure or line hygiene and should be investigated separately.

title: Cleaning sockets or cleaning bottles: which do I need?
summary: How cleaning sockets and cleaning bottles differ, how to match them to your couplers and how to look after them.
body: Q: What is a cleaning socket? A: A cleaning socket is fitted to a cleaning ring main in the cellar. During line cleaning, each keg coupler is connected to its socket instead of to a keg, so water and cleaning solution can be drawn through the lines. Sockets are made for each coupler type and have 3/8 inch JG fittings.

Q: What is a cleaning bottle? A: A heavy duty 5 litre bottle with a lid and dip tube that match a coupler type. It is filled with water or cleaning solution and pressurised by the gas supply to push the liquid around the system. It suits smaller installations and Lindr mobile units where there is no cleaning ring main.

Q: Can I use one cleaning socket or bottle for every coupler? A: No. Each socket or bottle only fits its own coupler type, just as each coupler only fits its own keg. You need one for every coupler type in use.
Q: I already have a cleaning bottle. Can I convert it for KeyKeg? A: A KeyKeg cap and tube is available for the 5 litre cleaning bottle. Check the bottle is in good condition before fitting it.

Q: How should I look after cleaning bottles? A: Rinse them after every use, store them empty with the lid off so they can dry, and inspect them for cracks, damaged threads or worn seals. Replace a damaged bottle rather than pressurising it.

title: Soda Pygmy soda water machine: regulator and installation questions
summary: Why the Soda Pygmy needs a specific regulator, what services it needs on site and how to keep it in good order.
body: Q: Can I use my existing beer gas regulator for the soda machine? A: No. The soda system requires a specific regulator. Tell Brewfitt when you order the machine so the correct regulator is supplied with it.

Q: What does the machine need on site? A: It makes chilled soda water by mixing drinking water with carbon dioxide, so it needs a drinking water supply, a CO2 cylinder secured upright with the correct regulator, and a suitable power supply. Follow the installation instructions in the operating manual.
Q: Who should connect it to the water supply? A: The connection must meet the water supply regulations, including backflow protection. Use a qualified plumber or installer if you are not certain.

Q: The soda water is flat. What should I check? A: Check the CO2 cylinder is not empty, the cylinder valve is open and the regulator is set as described in the manual. Then check the water supply is on. If the water is also warm, check the unit is running and its ventilation is clear.
Q: How often does it need cleaning? A: Clean the nozzles and drip tray daily, and sanitise the system at the intervals given in the manufacturer's instructions.

title: Energy Saviour Plug for beer and soft drink coolers: common questions
summary: What the Energy Saviour Plug is, which coolers it can be used with and what to check after fitting it.
body: Q: What is the Energy Saviour Plug? A: An app-controlled, power-saving plug-in device for beer and soft drink coolers. It is designed to reduce the energy a cooler uses.

Q: Which coolers can it be used with? A: Beer and soft drink coolers that run from a standard 13A UK mains socket. Hard-wired coolers are not suitable. If you are unsure how your cooler is connected, ask Brewfitt technical support.

Q: Will it affect the temperature of the beer? A: It is intended to save energy without affecting dispense quality. After fitting it, check dispense temperatures over the following week, including at your busiest times, and contact support if you notice any change.

Q: How do I set it up? A: Plug the device into the wall socket, plug the cooler into the device and follow the set-up steps in the app. Do not use it with extension leads or adaptors, and keep it dry and away from spills.
Q: How much will I save? A: Savings depend on the cooler, its age and condition, and how the site is used. The app lets you track the cooler's use so you can see the effect on your own site.

title: Nitro taps, nitro spouts and lager taps: what is the difference?
summary: How nitro and lager taps differ, when a nitro spout kit is enough, what compensator taps do and how to check a tap will fit your font.
body: Q: What makes a nitro tap different? A: Nitro taps are used for nitro and creamflow products such as stouts and smooth ales. They include a creamer plate, a small perforated disc that the beer is forced through, which releases nitrogen and forms the tight, creamy head those products need.

Q: Can I pour lager through a nitro tap? A: It is not recommended. The creamer plate knocks carbon dioxide out of lager and cider, leaving a flat, over-foamed pint. Use a lager tap for lager, beer and cider.

Q: Do I need a new tap to change a line from lager to nitro? A: Not always. Nitro spout kits are available for FC4 and Celtic taps, and a stainless steel nitro spout for Aceline taps. These screw on in place of the lager spout. Clean the tap thoroughly when changing over.

Q: What does a compensator tap do? A: A compensator lets you adjust the flow rate at the tap, which helps control foaming when pressure or line length is not ideal. Brewfitt stocks lager compensator taps and a nitro compensator tap suitable for Lindr dry cooler units.

Q: How do I know a tap will fit my font? A: Check the tap point on the font and the backshaft length in the tap description. Most taps in the range have a 1/2 inch backshaft and fit most fonts with a 1/2 inch tap point, and the tube connection size is shown in the product name. If in doubt, ask Brewfitt before ordering.

title: Ciocab hot drinks dispenser: getting started
summary: Basic questions about using the Ciocab bain-marie dispenser for hot chocolate, milk, mulled wine and tea, including daily cleaning.
body: Q: What can the Ciocab serve? A: It is designed for hot chocolate, milk, mulled wine and hot tea.

Q: How does it heat the drink without burning it? A: It uses a bain-marie, where water surrounding the product container is heated rather than the product itself. A vertical stirrer keeps the drink moving without creating foam, so the taste is preserved.

Q: What must I do before switching it on? A: Fill the bain-marie with water to the level described in the manufacturer's instructions. Never switch the heater on without water in the bain-marie, and site the unit on a stable surface away from the edge of the counter.

Q: How should dairy-based drinks be handled? A: Follow your food safety procedures for holding times and temperatures, and do not top up an old batch with fresh product. Empty and clean the container at the end of each service.

Q: How do I clean it? A: Switch off, unplug and allow the unit to cool before cleaning. Empty the product container, wash the container, lid, stirrer and tap parts in warm soapy water, rinse and dry them, and reassemble. Descale the bain-marie at the intervals given in the manual, particularly in hard water areas.

title: Handling beer line cleaning powder safely: common questions
summary: Safety questions from cellar staff about mixing, using and storing alkaline beer line cleaning powder.
body: Q: What protective equipment do I need? A: Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection whenever you handle the powder or the made-up solution. Make sure the product's safety data sheet is available in the cellar and that staff have read it.

Q: Can I make the solution stronger to clean dirty lines faster? A: No. Always use the dilution stated by the manufacturer. A stronger solution does not clean better and can damage seals and fittings and make rinsing harder. If lines are heavily soiled, ask for advice on a repeat clean.

Q: What should I do if solution gets on my skin or in my eyes? A: Follow the first aid instructions on the product label and safety data sheet straight away, rinsing with plenty of clean water, and seek medical advice where the instructions say so.

Q: Can I leave cleaning solution in the lines overnight? A: No. Leave it only for the contact time given by the manufacturer, then rinse the lines thoroughly with clean water. Never leave a line containing cleaner where it could be served.

Q: How should the sachets be stored? A: Keep them sealed, dry and in their original packaging, away from food, drink and acidic products, and out of reach of anyone who has not been trained to use them.

title: Changing the O-rings on an FC4 tap
summary: A short walkthrough showing how to strip down an FC4 tap, replace worn O-rings with the repair kit and put the tap back into service.
body: The video opens with the signs of worn O-rings: beer dripping from the spout after the tap is closed, weeping around the handle, or a stiff action. The presenter explains that a repair kit is quicker and cheaper than replacing the whole tap.

First the beer supply is isolated by turning off the secondary regulator for that line or disconnecting the coupler, and the tap is opened briefly over a bucket to release the pressure. The tap is then unscrewed from the font using the correct tap spanner, with a cloth to protect the chrome finish.

On the bench, the handle and spout are removed and the tap is dismantled in order, with each part laid out so it goes back the same way. The old O-rings are removed with a plastic pick rather than a sharp blade, so the seating surfaces are not scratched.

All parts are washed in warm water, the new O-rings from the kit are lightly coated with food-safe lubricant and fitted, and the tap is reassembled. The presenter checks the action moves freely before refitting.
Finally the tap is refitted to the font, the supply is restored and the joint is checked for leaks. The line is flushed and a few pours are discarded before the tap goes back into service.

title: Cleaning and packing a Lindr Kontakt unit after an event
summary: A walkthrough of the end-of-event routine for Lindr mobile units: flushing and cleaning the lines with a cleaning bottle, drying, and packing the unit safely for transport.
body: The presenter starts by switching off and unplugging the unit and closing the gas cylinder valve. Kegs are disconnected and the couplers are rinsed. Gloves and eye protection are worn from this point because cleaning solution is used.

A cleaning bottle with a lid matching the coupler type is filled with clean water, connected, and pressurised from the gas supply. Water is drawn through each tap until it runs clear. The bottle is then refilled with cleaning solution made up to the chemical supplier's instructions, drawn through, and left for the recommended contact time.

The lines are rinsed with clean water until no trace of cleaner remains, and then blown through with gas to push out as much water as possible. The taps are removed or opened and their spouts cleaned, and the drip tray is washed and dried.

For transport, the gas cylinder is removed and carried separately, secured upright in the vehicle. The unit is wiped down, ventilation openings are checked for debris, and it is strapped in the vehicle so it cannot slide or tip. The presenter recommends keeping the manual and a spare cleaning bottle with the unit.

title: Checking and topping up coolant in a Vision remote cooler
summary: A cellar walkthrough showing how to isolate a remote cooler, check the coolant reservoir, top up with pre-mixed coolant and spot the signs of a leak.
body: The video begins at the cooler isolator switch. The presenter explains that the cooler must be isolated before any cover is removed, and confirms the fans and pumps have stopped before going further.

The reservoir lid is removed and the coolant level is checked against the marks described in the cooler manufacturer's instructions. The presenter notes which coolant the system was commissioned with, which is usually recorded on a label or in the installation paperwork.
Pre-mixed coolant is added slowly to bring the level up to the correct mark. Gloves and eye protection are worn, and a cloth is kept ready for drips. The lid is refitted and the power restored.

The final section covers what to look for if the level keeps dropping: damp python insulation, drips below fonts, wet floors near the cooler and ice forming on fittings. The presenter advises contacting Brewfitt technical support rather than repeatedly topping up.

title: Converting a Celtic tap to nitro with a spout kit
summary: How to swap a Celtic lager spout for a nitro spout kit when a line changes from lager to a nitro or creamflow product, and how to change it back.
body: The presenter explains why nitro and creamflow products need a spout with a creamer plate, and shows the difference between the Celtic lager spout and the nitro spout kit side by side.
The line is isolated and the tap is closed. The lager spout is unscrewed by hand, and the tap body and threads are cleaned and checked for damage.
The nitro spout kit is screwed on by hand until it is snug, with the creamer plate seated correctly. The presenter warns against using tools on the spout, as over-tightening can damage the thread.

With the new product connected and the line cleaned, a test pour shows the creamy head a nitro spout produces. The presenter ends by reminding staff to label the tap and to refit the lager spout if the line is changed back, as lager poured through a creamer plate will be flat and over-foamed.

title: Installing and maintaining a Lindr AS under-counter ice bank cooler
summary: A walkthrough of positioning, filling and connecting a Lindr AS ice bank cooler to a tower, with routine maintenance checks for bar staff.
body: The video starts with siting the cooler: a level, well-ventilated position under the counter with the clearances shown in the Lindr installation instructions, away from glass washers and other heat sources. The presenter points out that restricted airflow is one of the most common reasons an ice bank cooler struggles in busy periods.

The water bath is filled with clean water to the level given in the manual before the unit is switched on. The cooler is then left to build its ice bank, which takes time, so the presenter recommends installing it the day before it is needed.

Product lines are connected from the couplers to the cooling coils and from the coils to the tower using the JG fitting kit, and the Lindr to tower connection kit is used where the cooler feeds a separate font. Every push-fit joint is checked by pulling gently on the tube.

For maintenance, the presenter shows how to isolate the power, check the water level, keep the condenser grille free of dust and look for a healthy ice bank. The water bath should be drained, cleaned and refilled at the intervals given in the manufacturer's instructions. Any fault with the refrigeration system should be referred to a qualified technician.

title: Setting up ColdFusion for nitro cold brew and cocktails
summary: A walkthrough of unpacking, positioning and preparing a ColdFusion nitro infusion unit, loading nitrogen and pouring the first drinks.
body: The video begins with unpacking the ColdFusion unit and choosing a position on the back bar that is stable, level, close to a power socket and with space around the ventilation openings.

The presenter shows how to fit a mini food grade nitrogen cylinder following the manufacturer's instructions, emphasising that only the specified cylinders should be used and that spare cylinders should be stored safely.

The product is prepared and chilled as recommended, and the unit is primed. The presenter pours several drinks to demonstrate the cascading effect and creamy head of a nitro infused drink, and explains that the product should be served straight away.
The final section covers daily cleaning: switching off, flushing the product path as the manual describes, cleaning the nozzle and drip tray, and leaving parts to dry overnight.

title: Changing a mini N2 nitrogen cylinder safely
summary: A short video showing how to recognise an empty mini nitrogen cylinder, replace it and dispose of used cylinders correctly.
body: The presenter explains how to tell when a mini nitrogen cylinder is running low, such as drinks losing their creamy head, and why the cylinder should be changed before service rather than during a busy period.

The equipment is switched off as described in its manual before the empty cylinder is removed. The presenter shows the cylinder being unscrewed by hand, noting that some residual gas may be released and that hands and face should be kept clear of the outlet.
A new food grade cylinder is checked for damage and fitted by hand until secure. The equipment is switched back on and a test drink is poured.

The video closes with storage and disposal advice: keep spare cylinders in a cool, dry place away from heat, never puncture or incinerate a cylinder, and follow the supplier's instructions for returning or recycling empty cylinders.
reviewNote: Checking the disposal section against the cylinder supplier's current returns guidance before publishing.

title: Connecting and disconnecting keg couplers safely
summary: A cellar demonstration of changing kegs with S, A, G and KeyKeg couplers, including checking the coupler seals and non-return valve.
body: The video opens with the presenter checking the new keg: confirming the coupler type, removing the dust cap and wiping the valve with a clean cloth. Kegs are moved with a sack truck or by rolling on the bottom rim, never by lifting on your own.

With the handle in the up position, the S type coupler is placed onto the keg valve, turned to lock it in place and the handle pressed down to open the valve. The presenter then shows the different connection actions for A type and G type couplers, and the KeyKeg coupler.
To disconnect, the handle is lifted to close the valve before the coupler is removed. The presenter points out that removing a coupler with the handle down can spray beer and damage the seals.
The last section shows how to inspect the coupler seal for cracks and swelling and how to check the non-return valve is present. Worn couplers should be taken out of service and replaced or repaired.
